title: Lesson 4 — Practice: Worked Exercises
summary: BBM140 Week 1 — practice problems with full solutions: capital from the accounting equation, a share issue, and two complete transaction-recording exercises (J&T football memorabilia shop and XTC company).

blocks.title: 🎯 Learning objectives
items: Use the accounting equation to find missing capital/equity.
Record a share issue that funds an asset purchase.
Work two full exercises: record transactions in a worksheet and prepare the balance sheet and income statement.
Handle capitalised acquisition costs, interest, advances from customers, and depreciation.

blocks.title: Warm-up 1 — How much capital?
blocks.content:
A business has a **property** worth £60,000, a **motor vehicle** worth £7,000, **inventory** worth £15,000 and **cash in the bank** of £6,000. It **owes £20,000** to suppliers, has a **bank overdraft of £2,000**, and **£3,000** is still outstanding on a **loan**. **How much capital (equity) does the business have?**

Use Equity = Assets − Liabilities.

blocks.title: Warm-up 2 — A share issue
blocks.content:
Continuing from the business above (assets 88,000; liabilities 25,000; equity 63,000):

> The firm **issues 6,000 new shares at £0.50 per share** and uses the money raised to **buy a piece of equipment**.

**How is this transaction recorded to keep the fundamental balance sheet equation in place?**

blocks.title: Warm-up 2 — Solution
blocks.content:
Money raised = 6,000 × £0.50 = **£3,000**. Two effects:
- **+£3,000 Equity** (share capital issued), and
- the cash raised is immediately spent, so **+£3,000 Fixed assets (equipment)**.

$$\Delta\text{Assets} = +3{,}000\ (\text{equipment}) \quad=\quad \Delta\text{Equity} = +3{,}000\ (\text{share capital})$$

Totals become **Assets 91,000 = Liabilities 25,000 + Equity 66,000**. The equation still holds. ✔

*(If the firm had kept the cash instead of buying equipment, the entry would be +3,000 cash = +3,000 share capital — same balancing idea.)*

blocks.title: Exercise A — J&T football memorabilia shop
blocks.content:
James and his brother Tom invest **£80,000 of cash** and **£20,000 of inventory** to start a football-memorabilia shop. During the year:

1. (Start-up) Invest £80,000 cash + £20,000 inventory.
2. A **shop costing £45,000** is acquired by paying **£12,500 in cash** and assuming a **10-year mortgage (loan)** for the rest, at **8%** yearly interest.
3. Merchandise costing **£36,000** is purchased **on account** from suppliers.
4. **Insurance** payment of **£200** for insurance coverage.
5. **Equipment costing £16,000** is purchased for cash.
6. Payment of **£200** to DHL for **delivering the equipment**.
7. Payment of **£24,000** to the suppliers of merchandise in (3).
8. Merchandise **costing £8,000** is **sold on credit for £18,000**.
9. **Salaries of £4,000** are paid to employees.
10. Payment of the **annual interest** on the loan.

**Required:** record the transactions in a worksheet, then prepare the **balance sheet** and **income statement** at year-end.

**Assumptions used in the solution:**
- The mortgage (loan) = 45,000 − 12,500 = **£32,500**; annual interest = 8% × 32,500 = **£2,600**.
- The **£200 DHL delivery** is a cost of bringing the equipment into use, so it is **capitalised** into Equipment (IAS 16) → equipment = £16,200.
- The insurance of £200 is treated as an **expense** of the year.

blocks.title: 🧪 Exercise A — worksheet solver (J&T)
blocks.prompt: Run the worksheet. It posts each transaction, checks the equation balances after every step, and prints the closing balances used for the statements. Try changing a number (e.g. the interest rate) and watch the profit change.
blocks.starter:
acc = {
    "Cash": 0, "Receivables": 0, "Stock": 0, "Building": 0, "Equipment": 0,  # assets
    "Payables": 0, "Loan": 0,                                                 # liabilities
    "Share capital": 0, "Profit": 0,                                          # equity
}
A = ["Cash", "Receivables", "Stock", "Building", "Equipment"]
L = ["Payables", "Loan"]
E = ["Share capital", "Profit"]

def post(label, **d):
    for k, v in d.items():
        acc[k] += v
    a, l, e = (sum(acc[k] for k in grp) for grp in (A, L, E))
    print(f"{label:26s} A={a:8.0f} L={l:7.0f} E={e:8.0f} {'OK' if abs(a-l-e)<1e-6 else 'OUT!'}")

post("1 Start-up",        Cash=+80000, Stock=+20000, **{"Share capital": +100000})
post("2 Buy shop",        Building=+45000, Cash=-12500, Loan=+32500)
post("3 Buy merchandise", Stock=+36000, Payables=+36000)
post("4 Insurance",       Cash=-200, Profit=-200)
post("5 Buy equipment",   Equipment=+16000, Cash=-16000)
post("6 Delivery (DHL)",  Equipment=+200, Cash=-200)   # capitalised
post("7 Pay suppliers",   Cash=-24000, Payables=-24000)
post("8 Sale on credit",  Receivables=+18000, Stock=-8000, Profit=+10000)
post("9 Salaries",        Cash=-4000, Profit=-4000)
post("10 Loan interest",  Cash=-2600, Profit=-2600)    # 8% x 32,500

print("\nClosing balances:")
for k, v in acc.items():
    print(f"  {k:14s} {v:9.0f}")

blocks.title: Exercise A — Solution: statements
blocks.content:
**Income statement (year 1)**

| | £ |
|---|---:|
| Sales revenue | 18,000 |
| Cost of sales | (8,000) |
| **Gross profit** | **10,000** |
| Insurance expense | (200) |
| Salaries expense | (4,000) |
| **Profit before interest** | **5,800** |
| Interest expense | (2,600) |
| **Profit for the year** | **3,200** |

**Balance sheet (year-end)**

| Assets | £ | Equity & Liabilities | £ |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| **Non-current assets** | | **Equity** | |
| Building | 45,000 | Share capital | 100,000 |
| Equipment | 16,200 | Retained profit | 3,200 |
| **Current assets** | | **Non-current liabilities** | |
| Inventory | 48,000 | Loan | 32,500 |
| Receivables | 18,000 | **Current liabilities** | |
| Cash | 20,500 | Accounts payable | 12,000 |
| **Total assets** | **147,700** | **Total equity & liabilities** | **147,700** |

The balance sheet balances at **£147,700**. ✔

blocks.title: Exercise B — XTC company
blocks.content:
XTC company started trading on **1 July, year 1**. Transactions during July:

- **1 Jul** — £130,000 cash contributed by owners, deposited in a bank account.
- **3 Jul** — Withdraw £6,000 from the current account to open a **3-month savings account**.
- **4 Jul** — Purchase **office equipment on credit for £10,000**, expected to be used over **10 years**.
- **5 Jul** — Purchase **£20,000 of merchandise on credit**.
- **7 Jul** — Pay a **£2,000 deposit** on a renting contract.
- **11 Jul** — Borrow **£5,000** on a bank credit line at **8%** annual interest.
- **14 Jul** — Receive a **£6,000 advance** from customers for future supplies.
- **16 Jul** — Pay **£12,000** to merchandise suppliers.
- **17 Jul** — **£6,000** of accounts payable is converted into a **note payable** due 30 August.
- **19 Jul** — **Settle the bank loan**; pay **one month's interest**.
- **23 Jul** — Credit sales: merchandise **£19,400** + services **£600** (cost of sales **£13,000**).
- **24 Jul** — **Interest received** on the savings account of **£275**.
- **26 Jul** — Pay **£1,000** monthly rent.
- **30 Jul** — Pay **£8,000** monthly salaries.
- **31 Jul** — Record **annual depreciation**.

**Assumptions used in the solution:**
- 'Cash & banks' combines the current and savings accounts, so the 3 Jul transfer nets to **£0**.
- The £2,000 deposit is an **asset** (recoverable), not an expense.
- One month's interest on the £5,000 loan = 8%/12 × 5,000 ≈ **£33**.
- Annual depreciation on equipment = 10,000 / 10 = **£1,000** (as the task asks for the *annual* charge).

blocks.title: 🧪 Exercise B — worksheet solver (XTC)
blocks.prompt: Run the worksheet for XTC. It checks the equation after every transaction and prints closing balances. Notice the business makes a small **loss** once depreciation and interest are included.
blocks.starter:
acc = {
    "Cash & banks": 0, "Receivables": 0, "Stock": 0, "Deposit": 0,
    "Equipment": 0, "Acc. depreciation": 0,                      # assets (acc.depr. is negative)
    "Payables": 0, "Advances": 0, "Note payable": 0, "Loan": 0,   # liabilities
    "Share capital": 0, "Profit": 0,                             # equity
}
A = ["Cash & banks", "Receivables", "Stock", "Deposit", "Equipment", "Acc. depreciation"]
L = ["Payables", "Advances", "Note payable", "Loan"]
E = ["Share capital", "Profit"]

def post(label, **d):
    for k, v in d.items():
        acc[k] += v
    a, l, e = (sum(acc[k] for k in grp) for grp in (A, L, E))
    print(f"{label:24s} A={a:9.0f} L={l:7.0f} E={e:9.0f} {'OK' if abs(a-l-e)<1e-6 else 'OUT!'}")

post("1 Owners' capital",  **{"Cash & banks": +130000, "Share capital": +130000})
post("3 Open savings",     **{"Cash & banks": 0})          # internal transfer -> net 0
post("4 Equipment (cr)",   Equipment=+10000, Payables=+10000)
post("5 Merchandise (cr)", Stock=+20000, Payables=+20000)
post("7 Rental deposit",   **{"Cash & banks": -2000, "Deposit": +2000})
post("11 Bank loan",       **{"Cash & banks": +5000, "Loan": +5000})
post("14 Customer advance",**{"Cash & banks": +6000, "Advances": +6000})
post("16 Pay suppliers",   **{"Cash & banks": -12000, "Payables": -12000})
post("17 Note payable",    Payables=-6000, **{"Note payable": +6000})
post("19 Settle loan",     **{"Cash & banks": -5033, "Loan": -5000, "Profit": -33})
post("23 Credit sales",    Receivables=+20000, Stock=-13000, Profit=+7000)
post("24 Interest income", **{"Cash & banks": +275, "Profit": +275})
post("26 Monthly rent",    **{"Cash & banks": -1000, "Profit": -1000})
post("30 Salaries",        **{"Cash & banks": -8000, "Profit": -8000})
post("31 Depreciation",    **{"Acc. depreciation": -1000, "Profit": -1000})

print("\nClosing balances:")
for k, v in acc.items():
    print(f"  {k:18s} {v:9.0f}")

blocks.title: Exercise B — Solution: statements
blocks.content:
**Income statement (July)**

| | £ |
|---|---:|
| Sales revenue (19,400 + 600) | 20,000 |
| Cost of sales | (13,000) |
| **Gross profit** | **7,000** |
| Interest income | 275 |
| Rent expense | (1,000) |
| Salaries expense | (8,000) |
| Depreciation expense | (1,000) |
| Interest expense | (33) |
| **Profit / (loss) for the period** | **(2,758)** |

**Balance sheet (31 July)**

| Assets | £ | Equity & Liabilities | £ |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| **Non-current assets** | | **Equity** | |
| Equipment (net of 1,000 depr.) | 9,000 | Share capital | 130,000 |
| **Current assets** | | Retained loss | (2,758) |
| Cash & banks | 113,242 | **Liabilities** | |
| Receivables | 20,000 | Accounts payable | 12,000 |
| Stock | 7,000 | Note payable | 6,000 |
| Rental deposit | 2,000 | Advances from customers | 6,000 |
| **Total assets** | **151,242** | **Total equity & liabilities** | **151,242** |

The balance sheet balances at **£151,242**, with equity = 130,000 − 2,758 = **£127,242**. ✔

> Even though a lot of cash came in, XTC made a small **loss** in its first month once cost of sales, salaries, rent, depreciation and interest are counted — a reminder that **cash ≠ profit**.

blocks.title: 📝 Recap
blocks.content: These exercises put Week 1 into practice. The accounting equation (Equity = Assets − Liabilities) finds missing capital; a share issue adds equity and (when spent) an asset, keeping the equation balanced. In the two full exercises we recorded every transaction in a worksheet — capitalising directly attributable costs (DHL delivery), computing loan interest, treating a customer advance as a liability and a rental deposit as an asset, reclassifying a payable into a note payable, and charging depreciation — then prepared the balance sheet and income statement. J&T made a £3,200 profit and balanced at £147,700; XTC made a small loss of £2,758 and balanced at £151,242, showing clearly that cash is not the same as profit.

blocks.title: 📖 Reference
blocks.content: *BBM140 Financial Reporting and Analysis — Week 1 exercises: 'J&T football memorabilia shop' and 'XTC company'.* Bayes Business School, City St George's, University of London. Solutions computed step-by-step; stated assumptions follow standard introductory treatment (IAS 16 for capitalised costs, IAS 2 for inventory).
